deities: Tara Chandi (Goddess Tara, a form of Durga/Shakti - depicted as a girl child, swayambhu)

history.summary: Maa Tara Chandi Temple at Chandanpur near Sasaram is the famous Shakti shrine of the Kaimur hill region: a natural-cave temple in the Kaimur Hills (Vindhya range) regarded as one of the 51 Siddha Shakta pithas - Puranic legend holds Sati's right eye (Netra) fell here. The self-manifested (swayambhu) goddess is depicted as a girl child in Tantric iconography: four-armed (knife and scissors in the right hands, hood and lotus in the left), lambodar, indigo-hued, tiger-skin clad, left foot forward on a corpse, per the District Rohtas official site. The Tara and Surya statues and a fragmentary Agni statue belong to the late/later Gupta period; a 12th-century inscription by the Kharwar king Mahanayak Pratap Dhavaldev's son Shatrudhan testifies to the deity's fame. She is the kuldevi of the Surwar Rajput (Gaur) royal family; local legend says Gautama Buddha visited after enlightenment and was guided toward Sarnath by the goddess. name: Maa Tara Chandi Temple
town_description: Sasaram is a historic city in Rohtas district of southwestern Bihar, best known for the grand tomb of Sher Shah Suri. It sits at the edge of the Kaimur Hills on the Grand Trunk Road (NH-19), a major railway junction and the gateway to the hill shrines of Tara Chandi, Gupta Dham, and the Manjhar Kund and Dhua Kund waterfalls.

travel.airport: Nearest airports: Varanasi (approximately 100 km), Gaya, and Patna (per the district administration site).
travel.railway: Sasaram Junction (SSM) - about 4-6 km from the temple.
travel.road: At Chandanpur on NH-19 (Grand Trunk Road) near Sasaram; shared autos and taxis run from the city center.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather and waterfalls; Navratri/Durga Puja for the biggest crowds. Morning 6:00 AM or evening 5:00 PM recommended for aarti.
